Learn endpoint paths, OAuth token setup, and key differences from CMS 12 and CMS 13.</p></div></header><div class="rm-Markdown markdown-body content-body" data-testid="RDMD"><style data-tailwind-stylesheet="true"></style><p>The CMS REST API is included in every CMS 13 project. The <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">AddCms()</span></code> method registers both the REST API v1 endpoints and the OAuth token endpoint, so no additional packages or registration calls are required to enable the API.</p>
<p>The CMS REST API is <strong>not</strong> intended for delivery. Optimizely recommends using <a target="_self" href="https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/digital-experience-platform/docs/optimizely-graph">Optimizely Graph</a> for content delivery.</p>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="api-endpoint-paths"></div><div class="heading-text">API endpoint paths</div><a aria-label="Skip link to API endpoint paths" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#api-endpoint-paths"></a></h2>
<p>CMS 13 exposes the REST API at the following base paths:</p>
<ul>
<li><button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">/_cms/v1</span></code> – The CMS REST API v1 root. Content, content type, and management endpoints are available under this path.</li>
<li><button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">/_cms/v1/oauth/token</span></code> – The OAuth token endpoint for requesting access tokens.</li>
</ul>
<p>The <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">AddCms()</span></code> method in your application startup calls <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">.AddOptimizelyCmsServiceV1().AddOauthEndpoints()</span></code>, which registers these endpoints. No additional service registration is needed.</p>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="rest-api-configuration-differences-from-cms-12-and-cms-13"></div><div class="heading-text">REST API configuration differences from CMS 12 and CMS 13</div><a aria-label="Skip link to REST API configuration differences from CMS 12 and CMS 13" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#rest-api-configuration-differences-from-cms-12-and-cms-13"></a></h2>
<p>CMS 13 simplifies REST API configuration compared to CMS 12 with Content Management and Content Definitions API. It does <strong>not</strong> replace the Content Delivery API.</p>
<p>While it is essentially the same API as CMS 13 exposes, there are some differences between the two.
The following table summarizes the differences.</p>
<div class="rdmd-table"><div class="rdmd-table-inner"><table><thead><tr><th>Area</th><th>CMS 12</th><th>CMS 13</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>API registration</td><td>Install <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">EPiServer.ContentManagementApi</span></code> and <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">EPiServer.ContentDefinitionsApi</span></code> NuGet packages and call <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code <h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="migrate-from-cms-12-authentication"></div><div class="heading-text">Migrate from CMS 12 authentication</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Migrate from CMS 12 authentication" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#migrate-from-cms-12-authentication"></a></h3>
<p>If you are upgrading from CMS 12 to CMS 13, replace the <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">EPiServer.OpenIDConnect</span></code> package configuration with the <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">CmsServiceOauthOptions</span></code> approach described in <a target="_blank" href="https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v13.0.0-CMS/reference/authentication-authorization-cms-rest-api" label="Authentication and authorization">Authentication and authorization</a>. CMS 13 does not require the <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">AddOpenIDConnect<ApplicationUser>()</span></code>, <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">AddContentManagementApi()</span></code>, or <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">AddContentDefinitionsApi()</span></code> calls. Instead, CMS 13 handles API registration and OAuth endpoint setup through <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">AddCms()</span></code>.</p>
<p>For CMS 12, the token endpoint was at <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">/api/episerver/connect/token</span></code>. In CMS 13, the token endpoint is at <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">/_cms/v1/oauth/token</span></code>.</p></div><div class="Footer-desktop1Hf-2fUBeoe2"><div align="center" class="Flex Flex_row " justify="between" style="--flex-gap: BodyMarkdown:
Introduction to the CMS REST API                                         

For AI agents: visit https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/llms.txt for an index of all pages formatted in Markdown and endpoints in OpenAPI.

The CMS REST API is included in every CMS 13 project. The `AddCms()` method registers both the REST API v1 endpoints and the OAuth token endpoint, so no additional packages or registration calls are required to enable the API.

The CMS REST API is **not** intended for delivery. Optimizely recommends using [Optimizely Graph](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/digital-experience-platform/docs/optimizely-graph) for content delivery.

## 

API endpoint paths

[](#api-endpoint-paths)

CMS 13 exposes the REST API at the following base paths:

*   `/_cms/v1` – The CMS REST API v1 root. Content, content type, and management endpoints are available under this path.
*   `/_cms/v1/oauth/token` – The OAuth token endpoint for requesting access tokens.

The `AddCms()` method in your application startup calls `.AddOptimizelyCmsServiceV1().AddOauthEndpoints()`, which registers these endpoints. No additional service registration is needed.

## 

REST API configuration differences from CMS 12 and CMS 13

[](#rest-api-configuration-differences-from-cms-12-and-cms-13)

CMS 13 simplifies REST API configuration compared to CMS 12 with Content Management and Content Definitions API. It does **not** replace the Content Delivery API.

While it is essentially the same API as CMS 13 exposes, there are some differences between the two. The following table summarizes the differences.

Area

CMS 12

CMS 13

API registration

Install `EPiServer.ContentManagementApi` and `EPiServer.ContentDefinitionsApi` NuGet packages and call `AddContentManagementApi()` and `AddContentDefinitionsApi()` in Startup.cs

Automatic with `AddCms()`, available at `/_cms/v1`

Authentication library

Install `EPiServer.OpenIDConnect` NuGet package and configure OpenIddict with ASP.NET Identity

Built-in OAuth at `/_cms/v1/oauth/token`, configured through `CmsServiceOauthOptions`

Client configuration

Define `OpenIDConnectApplication` objects in code with scopes and redirect URIs

Define clients in `appsettings.json` or environment variables with `ClientId` and `ClientSecret`

Signing credentials

Provide `X509Certificate2` manually or use `useDevelopmentCertificate: true`, DXP auto-provides through `CloudPlatform.Cms` 1.6.1 or later

DXP auto-provides through `AddCmsCloudPlatformSupport()`, local dev uses `AddDevelopmentSigningCredentials()`

Grant types supported

Authorization code, client credentials, resource owner password

Client credentials

Scope validation

Optional through `DisableScopeValidation`

Managed through client configuration

### 

Migrate from CMS 12 authentication

[](#migrate-from-cms-12-authentication)

If you are upgrading from CMS 12 to CMS 13, replace the `EPiServer.OpenIDConnect` package configuration with the `CmsServiceOauthOptions` approach described in [Authentication and authorization](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v13.0.0-CMS/reference/authentication-authorization-cms-rest-api). CMS 13 does not require the `AddOpenIDConnect<ApplicationUser>()`, `AddContentManagementApi()`, or `AddContentDefinitionsApi()` calls. Instead, CMS 13 handles API registration and OAuth endpoint setup through `AddCms()`.

For CMS 12, the token endpoint was at `/api/episerver/connect/token`. In CMS 13, the token endpoint is at `/_cms/v1/oauth/token`.
